rattle.title: Sonajero infantil
rattle.descTemplate: Los sonajeros están entre los juguetes sonoros más antiguos. En {country}, los cuidadores de {civ} llevan mucho tiempo sellando semillas o piedrecitas en calabaza, arcilla, cestería o madera para recompensar el agarre y el ritmo del bebé. El sonajero es a la vez juguete sensorial y, en algunos lugares, un sonido amuleto protector.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.
req: Sonajero hueco con semillas, piedrecitas o cascabeles

whistle_toy.title: Juguete silbato de arcilla o madera
whistle_toy.descTemplate: Los silbatos pequeños—arcilla en forma de pájaro, madera tallada, caña—aparecen en mercados y capas arqueológicas ligadas a la vida de {civ} en {country}. Los niños los usan como juguetes que amplifican la voz; algunos sirven también como ruidos de fiesta. El juego sonoro enseña respiración y tono de forma lúdica.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Juguete de animal de arrastre
pull_toy.descTemplate: Los animales con ruedas y figuras de arrastre están documentados desde la antigüedad clásica hasta las artesanías de aldea en {country}. Los artesanos de {civ} dan forma a caballos, aves o bueyes que enseñan a los toddlers a caminar sobre tracción y compañía en movimiento.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.
req: Figura animal con ruedas o deslizante

mini_weapons_toy.title: Set de arco o dardos de juguete
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Los juguetes de caza a escala dejan que los niños en {country} ensayen habilidades celebradas por los adultos de {civ}—tiro con arco, dardos de espina o cerbatana—con materiales más seguros. Las dianas de paja, madera o círculos dibujados convierten la técnica marcial en juego puntuado.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.
req: Arco o dardos de juguete blandos o de baja potencia

jacks_local.title: Piedras de habilidad de bolsillo
jacks_local.descTemplate: Más allá de la familia compartida de los huesecillos, {country} tiene secuencias locales de piedra y semilla moldeadas por la infancia de {civ}: distintos lanzamientos, cantos y escaleras de dificultad sobre el mismo principio de recoger, registradas aquí como práctica regional cuando cantos y secuencias son distintivos.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Juego de suertes / echar suertes narrativo
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Echar suertes para turnos, penitencias o consignas de historia aparece en reuniones de {civ} en {country}. Ya sean palitos de bambú, huesecillos o dados pintados, el azar elige quién habla, baila o responde: un juguete social entre la adivinación y el juego de fiesta.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Juego de figuras de sombra
shadow_play.descTemplate: El teatro de sombras—animales con las manos o títeres de cuero—ha entretenido las noches en {country} dentro de la narración de {civ}. Luz y silueta convierten el gesto en teatro. Algunas regiones lo elevaron a artes formales de títeres; las sombras de mano infantiles siguen siendo la forma juguete.
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Artesanía local de cometas
kite_local.descTemplate: Aunque volar cometas es una familia global, los artesanos de {civ} en {country} desarrollaron formas, papeles, bridones y usos festivos distintivos. Esta entrada destaca esa tradición artesanal local como práctica regional bajo el cielo más amplio de las cometas.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Muñeca de tela local
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Las muñecas blandas vestidas con patrones textiles locales aparecen en hogares de {civ} en {country}. Bordado, ropa envolvente y peinados miniaturizan el traje adulto. El juego de cuidados enseña roles sociales; las técnicas pasan entre generaciones.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Pelota de tela o cuero cosida
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Antes del caucho industrial, las comunidades de {civ} en {country} rellenaban y cosían pelotas de cuero, tela o fibra vegetal. Juegos de atrapar, patear y círculo crecieron en torno a estos objetos. La hechura de la pelota es tan cultural como las reglas.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.
req: Pelota cosida de tela, palma o cuero

top_local.title: Artesanía local de peonzas
top_local.descTemplate: El juego de peonza es antiguo y global; esta entrada registra estilos de talla, materiales de punta y etiqueta de concurso de {civ} en {country} como práctica distinta de oficio y juego dentro de ese juguete físico compartido.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Figuras de cuerda locales
string_local.descTemplate: Las figuras de cuerda de {civ} ligadas a {country} llevan nombres, animales y mitos locales aunque las aperturas se parezcan al cat's cradle de otros sitios. Las figuras son diagramas portátiles de relato y memoria de la mano.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Tablero de carrera folclórico (local)
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Los tableros de carrera en cruz y círculo aparecen en muchas tierras. En {country}, los jugadores de {civ} usaban conchas, palitos o huesecillos para llevar fichas a casa: primos de estructuras tipo pachisi pero con formas de pista y casillas seguras locales, registrados como tablero de carrera folclórico regional.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Siembra local de hoyos y semillas
sowing_local.descTemplate: Donde los juegos de siembra arraigaron en {country}, los tableros de {civ} muestran conteos de vasos, reglas de relevo y formas de madera distintivos. Pertenecen a la familia mancala pero merecen entradas regionales cuando la geometría del tablero y las costumbres de captura están estandarizadas localmente.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.
req: Tablero de vasos o hoyos en la tierra

jump_rope.title: Juegos de comba
jump_rope.descTemplate: Las rimas de saltar a la comba prosperan en patios y calles de {country} dentro de la cultura infantil de {civ}. Pasos de velocidad en solitario y juegos de cuerda larga en grupo comparten el ritmo del bote; los cantos localizan el juguete.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.
req: Cuerda de cáñamo, plástico o bejuco

blindfold_tag.title: La gallina ciega / juegos de llamada
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Los juegos de búsqueda con los ojos vendados—variantes de llamada y esquiva—aparecen en fiestas y reuniones infantiles de {civ} en {country}. El sonido, la quietud y la empatía hacia el jugador cegado estructuran la diversión.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Lucha folclórica juvenil
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Los juegos de lucha juvenil preparan para estilos folclóricos adultos celebrados por comunidades de {civ} en {country}. Las versiones de juego enfatizan derribos seguros, límites del círculo y risa por encima de la lesión: el deporte como juguete social.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: Canción de memoria / canto de eliminación
memory_song.descTemplate: Los cantos de eliminación y las canciones de memoria—parecidos a los juegos de círculo de «quién queda»—son juguetes de ritmo y atención en la cultura oral de {civ} en {country}. Palabras erróneas o tiempos fallidos eliminan jugadores hasta que queda uno.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Zancos o postes de equilibrio
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Los zancos aparecen como herramientas de fiesta y juguetes de equilibrio infantil en {country}. Los artesanos de {civ} elevan a los caminantes sobre bambú, madera o latas recicladas. Carreras y pasos de truco convierten la altura en juego.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.
req: Par de zancos o zancos de lata

leaf_boat.title: Carreras de barquitos de hoja o corteza
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Las carreras de barquitos miniatura con hojas, corteza o mazorcas deleitan a los niños cerca del agua en {country}. El juego de {civ} convierte las corrientes en pistas y la artesanía en experimentos de ingeniería.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.
req: Hojas, corteza o corcho para cascos

snow_or_sand.title: Juego de figuras de arena / nieve
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Esculpir figuras temporales en arena o nieve es juego de construcción elemental allí donde los paisajes de {civ} en {country} ofrecen el medio. Castillos, animales y formas ancestrales aparecen y se erosionan: arquitectura como juguete efímero.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Fútbol de mesa / fútbol de papel
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Los juegos de chasquido que simulan el fútbol sobre una mesa se extendieron por escuelas en {country}, sobre hábitos más antiguos de juguetes de dedo en la infancia de {civ}. Las porterías son libros o postes dibujados; los torneos pueden ser feroces.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.
req: Moneda, botón o bolita de papel

riddle_local.title: Intercambio local de acertijos
riddle_local.descTemplate: Los intercambios de acertijos en {country} preservan la metáfora, la ecología y el humor de {civ}. Plantear y resolver bajo presión de tiempo es un juguete mental que no requiere equipo fabricado.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Juguete sonajero de fiesta
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Los ruidosos de fiesta—matraca, castañuelas, palos de cascabel—dejan que los niños se unan a ritos públicos de {civ} en {country}. Volumen y ritmo marcan el tiempo del calendario; algunos juguetes son estacionales y se guardan después como equipo ritual.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.
req: Matraca, palo de cascabel, palmoteador o tambor juguete

puzzle_knot.title: Juguete de nudos y cordón
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Los puzles de desenredo de cordón, anillos y madera aparecen como juguetes de mercado y curiosidades de herrero en torno a {country}. Los jugadores de {civ} aprenden topología al tacto: liberar un anillo sin forzar y luego rearmar.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.
req: Puzle de cordón, anillos o alambre

mini_house.title: Set de juego de hogar en miniatura
mini_house.descTemplate: Las herramientas domésticas diminutas—cazuelas de barro, esteras tejidas, muebles de muñeca—sostienen el juego de roles de la vida doméstica adulta en las infancias de {civ} en {country}. Arqueología y etnografía hallan estos juguetes de enseñanza.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.
req: Ollitas, esteras o muñecas en miniatura

rattle.title: Hochets pour nourrissons
rattle.descTemplate: Les hochets comptent parmi les plus anciens jouets sonores. En {country}, les aidants de {civ} scellent depuis longtemps graines ou cailloux dans une calebasse, de l'argile, de la vannerie ou du bois pour récompenser la prise et le rythme du bébé. Le hochet est à la fois jouet sensoriel et, parfois, son d'amulette protectrice.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.
req: Hochet creux avec graines, cailloux ou clochettes

whistle_toy.title: Sifflet-jouet en argile ou bois
whistle_toy.descTemplate: De petits sifflets—argile en forme d'oiseau, bois sculpté, roseau—apparaissent sur les marchés et dans les couches archéologiques liées à la vie de {civ} en {country}. Les enfants s'en servent pour amplifier la voix ; certains deviennent aussi des bruiteurs de fête. Le jeu sonore enseigne souffle et hauteur avec légèreté.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Jouet animal à tirer
pull_toy.descTemplate: Animaux à roues et figures à tirer sont documentés de l'Antiquité classique aux artisanats villageois de {country}. Les artisans de {civ} façonnent chevaux, oiseaux ou bœufs qui enseignent aux tout-petits traction et compagnie en mouvement.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.
req: Figurine animale à roues ou glissante

mini_weapons_toy.title: Jeu d'arc ou fléchettes jouet
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Des jouets de chasse à l'échelle permettent aux enfants de {country} de répéter des savoir-faire célébrés par les adultes de {civ}—arc, fléchettes d'épine ou sarbacane—avec des matériaux plus sûrs. Cibles de paille, bois ou cercles dessinés transforment la technique martiale en jeu noté.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.
req: Arc/fléchettes jouet souples ou basse puissance

jacks_local.title: Pierres d'adresse de poche
jacks_local.descTemplate: Au-delà de la famille partagée des osselets, {country} a des séquences locales pierre-et-graine façonnées par l'enfance de {civ}—lancers, chants et échelles de difficulté distincts sur le même principe de ramassage, enregistrés ici comme pratique régionale quand chants et séquences sont localement distincts.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Tirage au sort / jeu de sorts narratifs
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Tirer au sort tours, gages ou amorces d'histoire apparaît dans les réunions de {civ} en {country}. Qu'il s'agisse de baguettes de bambou, d'osselets ou de dés peints, le hasard choisit qui parle, danse ou répond—un jouet social entre divination et jeu de fête.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Jeu de figures d'ombre
shadow_play.descTemplate: Le jeu d'ombres—animaux de main ou marionnettes de cuir—a diverti les nuits de {country} dans le récit de {civ}. Lumière et silhouette font du geste un théâtre. Certaines régions en ont fait des arts de marionnettes formels ; les ombres de main des enfants restent la forme jouet.
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Artisanat local de cerfs-volants
kite_local.descTemplate: Si voler un cerf-volant est une famille mondiale, les fabricants de {civ} en {country} ont développé formes, papiers, bridles et usages festifs distincts. Cette entrée met en avant cette tradition artisanale locale sous le ciel plus large des cerfs-volants.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Poupée de tissu locale
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Des poupées souples habillées aux motifs textiles locaux apparaissent dans les foyers de {civ} en {country}. Broderie, vêtements enveloppants et coiffures miniaturisent la tenue adulte. Le jeu de soin enseigne les rôles sociaux ; les techniques se transmettent.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Balle cousue de tissu ou peaux
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Avant le caoutchouc industriel, les communautés de {civ} en {country} bourraient et cousaient des balles de peau, tissu ou fibre végétale. Jeux de catch, coups de pied et cercles ont grandi autour de ces objets. La facture de la balle est aussi culturelle que les règles.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.
req: Balle cousue tissu, palmier ou peau

top_local.title: Artisanat local de toupies
top_local.descTemplate: Le jeu de toupie est ancien et mondial ; cette entrée consigne styles de sculpture, matériaux de pointe et étiquette de concours de {civ} en {country} comme pratique distincte d'artisanat et de jeu au sein de ce jouet physique partagé.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Figures de ficelle locales
string_local.descTemplate: Les figures de ficelle de {civ} liées à {country} portent noms, animaux et mythes locaux même si les ouvertures rappellent le cat's cradle ailleurs. Ce sont des diagrammes portables de récit et de mémoire de la main.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Plateau de course folklorique (local)
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Plateaux de course en croix et cercle apparaissent en bien des terres. En {country}, les joueurs de {civ} employaient coquillages, bâtonnets ou osselets pour ramener des pions à la maison—cousins des structures type pachisi mais avec formes de piste et cases sûres locales, consignés comme plateau de course folklorique régional.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Semis local à trous et graines
sowing_local.descTemplate: Là où les jeux de semis ont pris racine en {country}, les plateaux de {civ} montrent des nombres de coupes, règles de relais et formes de bois distincts. Ils appartiennent à la famille mancala mais méritent des entrées régionales quand géométrie et coutumes de capture sont localement standardisées.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.
req: Plateau à coupes ou trous dans la terre

jump_rope.title: Jeux de corde à sauter
jump_rope.descTemplate: Comptines et sauts à la corde prospèrent dans les cours et rues de {country} au sein de la culture enfantine de {civ}. Pas de vitesse en solo et jeux de longue corde en groupe partagent le rythme du rebond ; les chants localisent le jouet.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.
req: Corde de chanvre, plastique ou liane

blindfold_tag.title: Colin-maillard / jeux d'appel
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Jeux de quête les yeux bandés—variantes d'appel et d'esquive—apparaissent dans fêtes et réunions d'enfants de {civ} en {country}. Son, immobilité et empathie pour le joueur aveuglé structurent le plaisir.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Lutte folklorique pour la jeunesse
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Jeux de lutte jeunesse préparent aux styles folkloriques adultes célébrés par les communautés de {civ} en {country}. Les versions ludiques mettent l'accent sur projections sûres, limites du cercle et rire plutôt que blessure—le sport comme jouet social.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: Chanson de mémoire / comptine d'élimination
memory_song.descTemplate: Comptines d'élimination et chansons de mémoire—proches des jeux de cercle « qui reste »—sont des jouets de rythme et d'attention dans la culture orale de {civ} en {country}. Mots faux ou temps manqués éliminent jusqu'à ce qu'il n'en reste qu'un.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Échasses ou perches d'équilibre
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Les échasses apparaissent comme outils de fête et jouets d'équilibre enfants en {country}. Les fabricants de {civ} élèvent les marcheurs sur bambou, bois ou boîtes recyclées. Courses et pas de tour transforment l'élévation en jeu.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.
req: Paire d'échasses ou échasses de boîtes

leaf_boat.title: Course de bateaux de feuille ou d'écorce
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Courses de bateaux miniatures en feuilles, écorce ou épis enchantent les enfants près de l'eau en {country}. Le jeu de {civ} fait des courants des pistes et de l'artisanat des expériences d'ingénierie.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.
req: Feuilles, écorce ou liège pour coques

snow_or_sand.title: Jeu de figures de sable / neige
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Sculpter des figures temporaires dans le sable ou la neige est un jeu de construction élémentaire là où les paysages de {civ} en {country} offrent le médium. Châteaux, animaux et formes ancestrales apparaissent et s'érodent—architecture comme jouet éphémère.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Football de table / soccer en papier
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Jeux de pichenette simulant le football sur une table se sont répandus dans les écoles de {country}, sur des habitudes plus anciennes de jouets à doigts dans l'enfance de {civ}. Les buts sont des livres ou des poteaux dessinés ; les tournois peuvent être féroces.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.
req: Pièce, bouton ou boule de papier

riddle_local.title: Échange local d'énigmes
riddle_local.descTemplate: Les échanges d'énigmes en {country} préservent métaphore, écologie et humour de {civ}. Poser et résoudre sous pression temporelle est un jouet d'esprit sans matériel manufacturé.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Jouet bruiteur de fête
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Bruiteurs de fête—crécelles, claquoirs, bâtons à clochettes—laissent les enfants rejoindre les rites publics de {civ} en {country}. Volume et rythme marquent le temps du calendrier ; certains jouets sont saisonniers et rangés ensuite comme matériel rituel.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.
req: Crécelle, bâton à clochettes, claquoir ou tambour jouet

puzzle_knot.title: Jouet casse-tête de cordes et nœuds
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Casse-têtes de désenchevêtrement en corde, anneaux et bois apparaissent comme jouets de marché et curiosités de forgeron autour de {country}. Les joueurs de {civ} apprennent la topologie au toucher—libérer un anneau sans forcer, puis remonter.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.
req: Casse-tête de corde, anneaux ou fil

mini_house.title: Set de jeu de maison miniature
mini_house.descTemplate: Minuscules outils domestiques—poêlons d'argile, nattes tressées, meubles de poupée—soutiennent le jeu de rôle de la vie domestique adulte dans les enfances de {civ} en {country}. Archéologie et ethnographie trouvent ces jouets d'enseignement.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

rattle.title: Babyspielzeug-Rassel
rattle.descTemplate: Rasseln gehören zu den ältesten Klangspielzeugen. In {country} verschließen Betreuungspersonen von {civ} seit Langem Samen oder Kiesel in Kürbis, Ton, Flechtwerk oder Holz, um Greifen und Rhythmus des Säuglings zu belohnen. Die Rassel ist Sinnes-Spielzeug und mancherorts Schutzamulett-Klang.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.
req: Hohle Rassel mit Samen, Kieseln oder Glöckchen

whistle_toy.title: Ton- oder Holz-Pfeifenspielzeug
whistle_toy.descTemplate: Kleine Pfeifen—vogelgestaltiger Ton, geschnitztes Holz, Schilf—erscheinen auf Märkten und in archäologischen Schichten des Lebens von {civ} in {country}. Kinder nutzen sie als stimmenverstärkende Spielzeuge; manche sind auch Festlärmer. Klangspiel lehrt Atem und Tonhöhe spielerisch.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Tier-Ziehspielzeug
pull_toy.descTemplate: Räder-Tiere und Ziehfiguren sind von der klassischen Antike bis zu Dorfhandwerken in {country} belegt. Handwerker von {civ} formen Pferde, Vögel oder Ochsen, die Kleinkindern Zug und bewegte Gesellschaft beibringen.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: Spielbogen- oder Wurfpfeil-Set
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Verkleinerte Jagspielzeuge lassen Kinder in {country} Fertigkeiten üben, die Erwachsene von {civ} feiern—Bogen, Dornpfeile oder Blasrohr—mit sichereren Materialien. Ziele aus Stroh, Holz oder gezeichneten Kreisen machen Kampftechnik zum Punkte-Spiel.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: Taschen-Geschicklichkeitssteine
jacks_local.descTemplate: Jenseits der gemeinsamen Knöchelchen-Familie hat {country} lokale Stein-und-Samen-Folgen, geprägt von der Kindheit von {civ}—andere Würfe, Singsprüche und Schwierigkeitsleitern auf demselben Aufsammelprinzip, hier als regionale Praxis, wenn Sprüche und Folgen lokal eigen sind.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Losspiel / erzählendes Losziehen
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Lose ziehen für Züge, Strafen oder Geschichten-Anstöße erscheint in Versammlungen von {civ} in {country}. Ob Bambusstäbchen, Knöchelchen oder bemalte Würfel—der Zufall wählt, wer spricht, tanzt oder antwortet: ein soziales Spielzeug zwischen Orakel und Festspiel.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Schattenfiguren-Spiel
shadow_play.descTemplate: Schattenspiel—Handtiere oder Lederpuppen—hat Nächte in {country} im Erzählen von {civ} unterhalten. Licht und Silhouette machen Geste zum Theater. Manche Regionen erhoben dies zu formaler Puppenkunst; Kinderschatten mit der Hand bleiben die Spielzeugform.

kite_local.descTemplate: Während Drachensteigen eine globale Familie ist, entwickelten Macher von {civ} in {country} eigene Formen, Papiere, Bridles und Festnutzungen. Dieser Eintrag hebt jene lokale Handwerkstradition als regionale Drachenpraxis unter dem weiteren Drachenhimmel hervor.

cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Weiche Puppen in lokalen Textilmuster erscheinen in Haushalten von {civ} in {country}. Stickerei, Wickelkleidung und Frisuren verkleinern die Erwachsenentracht. Fürsorge-Spiel lehrt soziale Rollen; Techniken gehen über Generationen.

ball_sewn.descTemplate: Vor Industriegummi stopften und nähten Gemeinschaften von {civ} in {country} Bälle aus Haut, Stoff oder Pflanzenfaser. Fang-, Tritt- und Kreisspiele wuchsen um diese Objekte. Die Machart des Balls ist so kulturell wie die Regeln.

When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: Lokale Kreisel-Handwerkskunst
top_local.descTemplate: Kreiselspiel ist alt und global; dieser Eintrag hält Schnitzstile, Spitzenmaterialien und Wettkampfetikette von {civ} in {country} als eigene Handwerks-und-Spiel-Praxis innerhalb dieses gemeinsamen Physik-Spielzeugs fest.

string_local.title: Lokale Fadenspiele
string_local.descTemplate: Fadenspiele von {civ}, verbunden mit {country}, tragen lokale Namen, Tiere und Mythen, auch wenn Öffnungen dem Cat's Cradle anderswo ähneln. Die Figuren sind tragbare Diagramme von Geschichte und Handgedächtnis.

Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.

Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.descTemplate: Kreuz-und-Kreis- sowie Bahnen-Rennbretter erscheinen in vielen Ländern. In {country} nutzten Spieler von {civ} Muscheln, Stäbchen oder Knöchelchen, um Marker heimzubringen—Verwandte pachisi-artiger Strukturen, aber mit lokalen Bahnformen und Schutzfeldern, hier als regionales Volks-Rennbrett.
