Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Ἰκτῖνος τοπικός
kite_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ἰκτῖνος τοπικός» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Κόρη ὑφασμάτινη
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κόρη ὑφασμάτινη» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Σφαῖρα ῥαπτή
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σφαῖρα ῥαπτή» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: Στρόβιλος τοπικός
top_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Στρόβιλος τοπικός» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Σχήματα μίτου
string_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σχήματα μίτου» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Πίναξ δρόμου δημώδης
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πίναξ δρόμου δημώδης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Σπορὰ τοπική
sowing_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σπορὰ τοπική» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: Σχοινίον πηδητικόν
jump_rope.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Σχοινίον πηδητικόν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: Παιδιὰ τετυφλωμένα
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Παιδιὰ τετυφλωμένα» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Πάλη δημώδης
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πάλη δημώδης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: ᾨδὴ μνήμης
memory_song.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «ᾨδὴ μνήμης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Κάλτιοι
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κάλτιοι» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: Πλοιάρια φύλλων
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Πλοιάρια φύλλων» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: Μορφαὶ ἄμμου/χιόνος
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Μορφαὶ ἄμμου/χιόνος» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Ποδόσφαιρον τραπέζης
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Ποδόσφαιρον τραπέζης» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: Αἰνίγματα τοπικά
riddle_local.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Αἰνίγματα τοπικά» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Κρόταλον ἑορταστικόν
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Κρόταλον ἑορταστικόν» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: Αἴνιγμα κόμβων
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Αἴνιγμα κόμβων» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: Οἰκίσκος
mini_house.descTemplate: Τὸ παίγνιον «Οἰκίσκος» ἐν {country} κατὰ τὸν βίον τοῦ {civ} μαρτυρεῖται. Ἡ τοπικὴ μορφὴ διδάσκει τέχνας κοινωνικὰς καὶ σωματικάς. Ὕλαι καὶ ἔθη διαφέρουσιν.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

rattle.title: शिशुघण्टिका
rattle.descTemplate: «शिशुघण्टिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: मृत्तिकाकाष्ठसीत्कारकम्
whistle_toy.descTemplate: «मृत्तिकाकाष्ठसीत्कारकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: आकृष्यमाणपशुक्रीडनकम्
pull_toy.descTemplate: «आकृष्यमाणपशुक्रीडनकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: क्रीडनधनुः
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: «क्रीडनधनुः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: कौशलपाषाणाः
jacks_local.descTemplate: «कौशलपाषाणाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: कथाभाग्याः
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: «कथाभाग्याः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: छायाक्रीडा
shadow_play.descTemplate: «छायाक्रीडा» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: स्थानीयपतङ्गः
kite_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयपतङ्गः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: वस्त्रपुत्तलिका
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: «वस्त्रपुत्तलिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: सीव्यमानकन्दुकः
ball_sewn.descTemplate: «सीव्यमानकन्दुकः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: स्थानीयभ्रमरः
top_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयभ्रमरः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: स्थानीयसूत्ररूपाणि
string_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयसूत्ररूपाणि» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: लोकधावनफलकम्
board_race_folk.descTemplate: «लोकधावनफलकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: स्थानीयवपनम्
sowing_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयवपनम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: रज्जुप्लवनम्
jump_rope.descTemplate: «रज्जुप्लवनम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: अन्धपटक्रीडा
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: «अन्धपटक्रीडा» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: लोकमल्लयुद्धम्
wrestling_play.descTemplate: «लोकमल्लयुद्धम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: स्मृतिगीतम्
memory_song.descTemplate: «स्मृतिगीतम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: पादकाष्ठानि
balance_stilts.descTemplate: «पादकाष्ठानि» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: पर्णनौकाः
leaf_boat.descTemplate: «पर्णनौकाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: सिकताहिममूर्तयः
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: «सिकताहिममूर्तयः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: फलकपादकन्दुकः
knuckle_football.descTemplate: «फलकपादकन्दुकः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: स्थानीयप्रहेलिकाः
riddle_local.descTemplate: «स्थानीयप्रहेलिकाः» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: उत्सवनादकम्
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: «उत्सवनादकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: ग्रन्थिप्रहेलिका
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: «ग्रन्थिप्रहेलिका» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: लघुगृहक्रीडनकम्
mini_house.descTemplate: «लघुगृहक्रीडनकम्» इति क्रीडनकं {country} देशे {civ} संस्कृतौ प्रसिद्धम्। स्थानीयस्वरूपेण बालाः कौशलान् क्रीडया शिक्षन्ते। द्रव्याणि रीतयश्च भिद्यन्ते।
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

rattle.title: sšš.t n ẖrd (infant rattle)
rattle.descTemplate: sšš.t n ẖrd (infant rattle). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: sḏm-ḫrt (whistle toy)
whistle_toy.descTemplate: sḏm-ḫrt (whistle toy). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: ṯꜣy stꜣ (pull animal)
pull_toy.descTemplate: ṯꜣy stꜣ (pull animal). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: pḏt šrr (toy bow)
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: pḏt šrr (toy bow). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: ꜥꜣt n ḫbꜥ (skill stones)
jacks_local.descTemplate: ꜥꜣt n ḫbꜥ (skill stones). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: šꜣy.t sḏd (story lots)
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: šꜣy.t sḏd (story lots). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: šwt ḫprw (shadow play)
shadow_play.descTemplate: šwt ḫprw (shadow play). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: ꜥpꜣy n tꜣ (local kite)
kite_local.descTemplate: ꜥpꜣy n tꜣ (local kite). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: sšn n dmỉ (cloth doll)
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: sšn n dmỉ (cloth doll). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: ḥbn.t n dmỉ (sewn ball)
ball_sewn.descTemplate: ḥbn.t n dmỉ (sewn ball). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)

Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.descTemplate: ptpt n dmỉ (local top). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)

Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: nwḥ ḳd (string figures)
string_local.descTemplate: nwḥ ḳd (string figures). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)

Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.descTemplate: snṯ n dmỉ (folk race board). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.

sowing_local.title: stỉ n dmỉ (local sowing)
sowing_local.descTemplate: stỉ n dmỉ (local sowing). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: nwḥ n ḫbꜥ (jump rope)
jump_rope.descTemplate: nwḥ n ḫbꜥ (jump rope). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: ḫꜣy.t ḳmꜣ (blindfold games)
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: ḫꜣy.t ḳmꜣ (blindfold games). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: ḳnḳn n ẖrdw (youth wrestling)
wrestling_play.descTemplate: ḳnḳn n ẖrdw (youth wrestling). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: ḥsı͗ n sḫꜣ (memory song)
memory_song.descTemplate: ḥsı͗ n sḫꜣ (memory song). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: rdwy ḳꜣ (stilts)
balance_stilts.descTemplate: rdwy ḳꜣ (stilts). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: dpt n ḫꜣw (leaf boats)
leaf_boat.descTemplate: dpt n ḫꜣw (leaf boats). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: twt n šꜥ/snw (sand/snow figures)
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: twt n šꜥ/snw (sand/snow figures). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: ḥbn.t n wdḥw (table flick ball)
knuckle_football.descTemplate: ḥbn.t n wdḥw (table flick ball). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).

Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.descTemplate: ṯnı͗w n dmỉ (local riddles). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).

A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.

First to five points wins the exchange.

steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.descTemplate: ts n snṯ (knot puzzle). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.descTemplate: pr šrr (miniature house). Play custom of {country} within {civ}. Local materials teach children skills; forms vary by household. (r n kmt scholarly gloss)
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

rattle.title: šaḫḫarru ša šerri (infant rattle)
rattle.descTemplate: šaḫḫarru ša šerri (infant rattle). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: ḫalḫallatu ṣeḫertu (whistle toy)
whistle_toy.descTemplate: ḫalḫallatu ṣeḫertu (whistle toy). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: būlu ša šadādu (pull animal)
pull_toy.descTemplate: būlu ša šadādu (pull animal). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: qaštu ṣeḫertu (toy bow)
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: qaštu ṣeḫertu (toy bow). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: abnū nemequ (skill stones)
jacks_local.descTemplate: abnū nemequ (skill stones). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: pūru ša amātu (story lots)
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: pūru ša amātu (story lots). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: ṣillu mēlultu (shadow play)
shadow_play.descTemplate: ṣillu mēlultu (shadow play). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: iṣṣūru ša šāru (local kite)
kite_local.descTemplate: iṣṣūru ša šāru (local kite). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: ṣalamu ša ṣubātu (cloth doll)
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: ṣalamu ša ṣubātu (cloth doll). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: kakku tarṣu (sewn ball)
ball_sewn.descTemplate: kakku tarṣu (sewn ball). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)

Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: ṣâdu ašru (local top)
top_local.descTemplate: ṣâdu ašru (local top). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: qû ṣalamū (string figures)
string_local.descTemplate: qû ṣalamū (string figures). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: lēʾu lasāmu (folk race board)
board_race_folk.descTemplate: lēʾu lasāmu (folk race board). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: bītu ṣeḫru (miniature house)
mini_house.descTemplate: bītu ṣeḫru (miniature house). In {country} among {civ}, this mēlultu (play) is noted. Children learn turn-taking; craft follows local unūtu. (Akkadian scholarly gloss)
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.

rattle.title: Barnahristingr
rattle.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Barnahristingr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: In {country}, offer a sealed {civ} rattle (gourd, clay, wood, or basketry with seeds or pebbles) within the infant’s supervised reach.
Shake once slowly so the child hears a clear cause-and-effect sound, then pause for them to grasp.
Allow grasping, gentle shaking, and dropping onto a soft mat; block mouthing if the shell cracks or finishes flake.
Sing or speak a short {civ} lullaby or counting rhyme from {country} in time with three to five shakes.
After each session, check seams, plugs, and loose bits; retire the toy if seeds can spill.

whistle_toy.title: Leikflauta
whistle_toy.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Leikflauta» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Hold a clay, wood, or reed whistle made in the {civ} craft style of {country}; keep finger holes and the windway clear.
Blow a steady stream for two seconds to find one clear tone before trying short chirps.
Alternate three short calls and one long note; count successful clear tones aloud.
Play call-and-response with a partner: one player blows a rhythm from {country} street or festival play, the other copies it.
Wash or wipe the mouthpiece between players; do not share if anyone is ill.

pull_toy.title: Dýradráttarleikr
pull_toy.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Dýradráttarleikr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Tie a short cord to the nose or yoke of a wheeled {civ} animal figure from {country}; leave enough slack for a toddler’s stride.
Walk five to ten steps on a clear floor so wheels or runners follow without tipping.
Make one gentle left turn and one right turn; stop if the axle binds or the cord jerks the toy airborne.
Narrate a short parade or market delivery story using animals familiar in {country} (horse, ox, bird, or camel as fits the figure).
Coil the cord after play and store the toy upright so wheels stay round.

mini_weapons_toy.title: Leikbogi
mini_weapons_toy.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Leikbogi» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Outdoors in {country}, set a straw, wood, or chalk target with a backstop; clear people and animals for at least five paces downrange.
Nock a soft arrow or load a foam/cork dart; keep the tip pointed at the ground until ready.
Use a calm {civ} stance—feet apart, eyes on the center ring—and release one shot at a time.
Score 3 points for the center, 2 for the middle ring, 1 for the outer; first to 15 points wins a round.
Never aim at people or animals; collect every projectile before the next turn.

jacks_local.title: Fimrasteinar
jacks_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Fimrasteinar» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Sit on flat ground in {country} with five small stones or seeds used in {civ} children’s pickup play.
Scatter all five lightly, then toss one skyward and pick up exactly one stone before catching the tossed stone.
On the next turns, pick up two, then three, then the last group of remaining stones in one sweep while the toss is aloft.
Drop or fail to catch ends your turn; the next player restarts at ones.
First player to finish the ones–twos–threes–fours ladder while saying a short {civ} count or chant from {country} wins.

story_dice_oral.title: Sögukostir
story_dice_oral.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Sögukostir» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Put three to six marked sticks, shells, or dice in a cup—marks can be colors or short {civ} prompt words used in {country}.
Shake once and cast onto a cloth; read the uppermost mark as this turn’s prompt.
The indicated player has thirty seconds to tell a short story, sing one verse, or perform a playful forfeit named by the mark.
Return all lots to the cup and pass clockwise until each player has had at least two turns.
Before starting, list which marks are playful only—never use sacred {civ} divination lots from {country} as party toys.

shadow_play.title: Skuggaleikr
shadow_play.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Skuggaleikr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: In a dim room in {country}, place a lamp or candle so hands cast sharp shadows on a blank wall about one arm’s length away.
Form one animal or person with fingers; move slowly for three seconds so the outline stays readable.
Narrate a one-minute {civ} folk scene (market, animal chase, or hero greeting) while the shadow acts.
Optional: cut a cardboard figure, tape it to a stick, and replay the same scene with crisper edges.
End by letting each child invent one new creature and name it before the lamp is put out.

kite_local.title: Staðarflugdreki
kite_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Staðarflugdreki» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Build or buy a paper or cloth kite in a shape used by {civ} makers in {country} (diamond, box, bird, or fighter flat).
Check that both bridle legs are equal and the spar joints are tight before you walk to the field.
Stand with the wind at your back in open ground; have a helper release the kite as you take three steps and feed five to ten meters of line.
Steer by tension: pull to climb, ease to dive; land by walking toward the kite while reeling.
Never fly near power lines, airports, or storms—common safety rules for festival kite days in {country}.

cloth_doll_local.title: Local cloth doll
cloth_doll_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Klæðisbrúða» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Sew or tie a simple cloth body and stuff it firmly with fiber so the head and torso hold shape.
Dress the doll in miniature wraps, sash, or embroidered scraps that echo everyday {civ} clothing in {country}.
Act out at least three caregiving scenes: wake, feed, and put to sleep.
Repair tears with needle and thread as part of play rather than discarding the doll.
No points are scored—nurture play ends when the child packs the doll into a small basket or box used in {country} households.

ball_sewn.title: Saumaðr bolti
ball_sewn.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Saumaðr bolti» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Form a circle of four or more players in a clear yard in {country}; use one sewn cloth, palm-fiber, or hide ball.
Toss underhand to the neighbor on your right; {civ} circle play scores one point for each clean catch.
A drop removes that player from the circle (or gives the thrower one point if you play pairs).
When three players remain, speed up to a one-second hold before passing.
Last player in the circle wins; restart with everyone after one champion round.

top_local.title: Staðarsnúðr
top_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Staðarsnúðr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Wind a cord clockwise around a carved {civ} top from {country}, or ready a short whip cord if the tip is meant for whipping.
Plant your feet on hard earth or stone; pull the cord smooth and level so the tip bites and spins.
For whip tops, tap the shoulder of the top lightly to keep it upright for a timed spin.
In a contest, longest continuous spin wins; or play combat where the first top knocked flat loses.
Sand a dull tip and re-point it before the next match so launches stay true.

string_local.title: Staðarþráðarmyndir
string_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Staðarþráðarmyndir» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Make a loop of cord about the span of your outstretched arms so it fits both hands with slight slack.
Open on both thumbs and little fingers in the starting position taught for {civ} figures in {country}.
Pick, drop, and transfer strings until you hold one named figure (animal, tool, or star) for three seconds.
Say the figure’s {civ} name or a one-sentence story tied to {country} while holding the shape.
Teach that single figure to a partner before starting a second pattern.

board_race_folk.title: Þjóðkapphlauptafl
board_race_folk.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Þjóðkapphlauptafl» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Seat 2–4 players at a path or cross-and-circle board used in {country}; each gets four markers in a starting nest.
Throw two casting sticks, four cowrie shells, or one die—whatever {civ} sets use—and total the pips or “mouth-up” shells.
Enter a marker only on a throw of the highest single result (for example 4 sticks or a 6); then advance that many spaces.
Landing on an opponent’s single marker sends it back to its nest; stacked markers are safe.
First player to move all four markers around the track and into the home column wins.

sowing_local.title: Staðarsáðleikr
sowing_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Staðarsáðleikr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Use a 2×6 board (twelve small pits plus one store per side) common in {civ} sowing play in {country}; place four seeds in each small pit.
On your turn, scoop every seed from one pit on your side and sow one seed into each following pit counterclockwise, including your store but skipping the opponent’s store.
If the last seed lands in your empty pit and the opposite pit holds seeds, capture those opposite seeds into your store.
If the last seed lands in your store, take another turn; otherwise play passes.
When one side’s pits are empty, the opponent puts remaining seeds in their store; most seeds in store wins.

jump_rope.title: Hoppreip
jump_rope.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Hoppreip» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: For solo play: hold both ends, swing the rope over your head, and jump once per pass; count consecutive jumps.
For group play: two turners swing a long rope; a jumper runs in, jumps five times, and runs out.
Add a short {civ} schoolyard chant from {country}; a missed jump or broken rhythm rotates the jumper to turner.
Try pepper (fast turns) or one double-under after you can clear twenty steady jumps.
Keep the rope away from roads, wet floors, and low branches.

blindfold_tag.title: Blindisleikr
blindfold_tag.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Blindisleikr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Clear toys and furniture from a bounded room or yard in {country}; mark walls or chalk lines as out-of-bounds.
Blindfold one seeker and spin them twice; sighted players must stay inside the bounds.
Sighted players may call a short {civ} nickname or clap once every five seconds so the seeker has sound cues.
The seeker tags by touch; the tagged player becomes the next seeker.
Stop the round immediately if anyone near stairs or hard edges; remove the blindfold before leaving the space.

wrestling_play.title: Þjóðglíma ungra
wrestling_play.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Þjóðglíma ungra» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Mark a circle about three paces across on sand or soft ground used for youth bouts in {country}.
Forbid headlocks, joint twists, and strikes; wrestlers may grip belts, sashes, or shoulders as in {civ} play wrestling.
A referee starts each exchange; first to make the opponent’s knee or back touch outside or flat wins that exchange.
Best of three exchanges decides the bout; rest thirty seconds between exchanges.
Handshake or salute after the bout; the referee ends play at the first sign of pain.

memory_song.title: Minnissöngr
memory_song.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Minnissöngr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Stand or sit in a circle so every player can see the leader’s hands.
The leader starts a {civ} elimination chant or clapping song known in {country}, with one word or beat per player.
Each player must say the next word or clap on the next beat without pausing more than one second.
A wrong word, late beat, or broken gesture eliminates that player, who steps back one pace.
Last remaining player wins and leads the next round’s chant.

balance_stilts.title: Stolpar
balance_stilts.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Stolpar» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Mount bamboo, wood, or tin-can stilts built in the {civ} style of {country} with a spotter holding your elbow.
Take ten small steps on level ground while looking forward, not down at the footrests.
Race a marked ten-meter line, or walk a chalk zigzag without a footrest touching the ground.
Dismount by stepping backward onto clear ground with the spotter ready.
Check cords, cans, and footrest bindings before every session; replace frayed ties.

leaf_boat.title: Laufbátar
leaf_boat.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Laufbátar» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Fold a broad leaf or carve a bark/cork hull that floats—materials children gather near water in {country}.
Mark a start and finish about two meters apart in a basin or gentle gutter current.
On a shared count of three in any {civ} counting words, release all boats together; no pushing after release.
First boat to touch the finish line wins the heat; run best of three heats.
Retrieve every leaf, twig, and cork; leave the water clear of trash.

snow_or_sand.title: Sand-/snjómyndir
snow_or_sand.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Sand-/snjómyndir» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Gather moist sand or packable snow from a safe open patch in {country}—never dig undercut cliffs.
Pile a base, then carve one figure or fort wall with hands or a simple mold.
Optional contest: tallest free-standing tower in five minutes, or best likeness of an animal known in {civ} stories.
Photograph if you wish, then watch or gently collapse the build as part of play.
Stay off sacred dunes, marked ruins, and protected sites; fill holes you dig on public beaches.

knuckle_football.title: Borðknattleikr
knuckle_football.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Borðknattleikr» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: On a clear table in {country}, mark each goal with two small gaps about three finger-widths wide (books or tape posts).
Place a coin, button, or crumpled paper ball on the center line.
Players alternate one finger-flick; no covering the ball with a palm—common {civ} school-desk rule.
A goal scores when the ball fully crosses between the posts; play to five goals.
If the ball leaves the table, the opponent places it back one hand-span from the edge and flicks next.

riddle_local.title: Staðargátur
riddle_local.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Staðargátur» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: One player poses a riddle drawn from {civ} oral tradition in {country} (animals, tools, weather, or food metaphors).
Others have one minute and up to three guesses.
A correct solver scores one point and poses the next riddle; if no one solves, the poser scores one point and chooses the next poser.
Optional playful forfeit for three wrong guesses: clap a rhythm or name five animals from ${c}.
First to five points wins the exchange.

ceremonial_toy.title: Hátíðarhljóðfæri
ceremonial_toy.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Hátíðarhljóðfæri» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Ask an adult when ratchets, clappers, or bell-sticks are welcome in the {civ} festival calendar of {country}.
Play short pulses that match the procession drum or sung phrase—typically two or four beats per measure.
Stop instantly when ceremony leaders raise a hand or the song falls silent.
Do not imitate restricted sacred instruments or mock prayer gestures with the toy.
Wipe the handle clean and store the noisemaker until the next public festival day.

puzzle_knot.title: Hnútugáta
puzzle_knot.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Hnútugáta» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Study a cord-and-ring or wire puzzle sold or forged around {country}; note which loop is the piece you must free.
Move loops only through openings that already exist—do not bend metal or force wood.
Free the target ring or block by a legal path; {civ} market puzzles are solved when that piece separates cleanly.
Reassemble every loop to the exact starting state before claiming the solve.
Time your solve, then challenge a friend to beat that time with the same path.

mini_house.title: Smáhús
mini_house.descTemplate: Leikrinn «Smáhús» er kunnugr í {country} meðal {civ}. Staðbundin efni kenna börnum hæfni; útfærslur breytast eftir svæðum.
steps: Arrange miniature pots, mats, and dolls into a small hearth or room layout familiar in {country}.
Assign roles (cook, guest, child) to dolls or players before the scene starts.
Act out one cooking scene, one market or visiting scene, and one bedtime scene drawn from {civ} daily life.
Add one new prop each week (ladle, basket, or stool) and reuse it in the next story.
Pack all pieces into one box after play so the set stays complete.
